findings.title: Dynamic imports in appStore are evaluated eagerly at module load time
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each entry in `appStore` is defined as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` rather than a factory function like `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`. Because `import(...)` is called directly when constructing the `appStore` object literal, all 28 app modules are still imported immediately as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported anywhere, rather than lazily loading only the needed app on demand. Additionally, if any unused app module fails to load at startup, it will produce an unhandled promise rejection.

findings.title: Async forEach callback pushes to apiDeletes after Promise.all is already called
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining bookings in a recurring series (`allRemainingBookings` at lines 458-470), `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` is used. Because `forEach` does not await its async callback, execution immediately continues past the `if (bookingCalendarReference)` block right after hitting `await getCalendar(credential)`. By the time `getCalendar` and `calendar.deleteEvent` resolve inside the callback, `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 (or `await apiDeletes` at line 617) has already been invoked on an array that does not contain those delete promises, so the calendar deletions are not awaited before the handler returns and any rejections go unhandled.

findings.title: Async forEach inside try/catch neither awaits deletions nor catches errors
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` is wrapped in a `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` block. Because `forEach` ignores the promises returned by the async callback, `Reschedule` does not wait for `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` to finish before sending emails and returning, and any error thrown after the first `await` will become an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

findings.title: Async forEach inside try/catch neither awaits deletions nor catches errors
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` is wrapped in a `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` block. Because `forEach` does not await the promises returned by its async callback, calendar and video deletions run detached in the background and any rejection after `await getCalendar(...)` bypasses the `try/catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials starts getCalendar promises for non-calendar variants and discards them
findings.body: In `getCalendarCredentials`, `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` is called before checking `app.variant === "calendar"`. Now that `getCalendar` is `async` and returns a `Promise`, calling it unconditionally starts an async operation for every credential of any app whose type ends with `_calendar` (such as `closecom_other_calendar` or `wipemycalother`), and if `app.variant !== "calendar"`, the returned promise is immediately discarded without a rejection handler. `getCalendar(credential)` should only be called when `app.variant === "calendar"`.
